The test image shows a corn stalk segment with **numerous tiny black dots** scattered densely across a tan/brown surface. Key observations:
- Stalk tissue (not a leaf)
- Countless tiny black specks/dots on the external rind
- Tan-brown coloration of stalk surface

Top candidates: **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (small black pycnidia on lower internodes), **Charcoal_stalk_rot** (tiny black sclerotia), **Tar_spot** (black raised structures — but usually on leaves).

Let me view reference images for the top candidates in parallel:
Charcoal stalk rot shows internal shredded gray pith. Tar spot is on leaves. Diplodia reference shows lodged stalks but not clear pycnidia close-up. Let me check more candidates:

Key observations so far:
- Anthracnose stalk rot shows shiny black patches (not tiny dots)
- Physoderma brown spot bottom-right shows dense tiny black dots on midrib — similar pattern!
- Physoderma stalk rot shows black nodes

Let me view a few more to confirm:

Looking at the Common rust bottom-right panel — shows dense tiny black dots on a tan stalk surface, very similar! Tar spot bottom-right also shows a tan/brown surface with black dots.

Let me view a few more critical comparisons:

Now I have enough evidence to make my assessment. Let me analyze:

**Test image**: Cylindrical stalk segment, tan-brown, completely covered with hundreds of very tiny, uniform black dots on the exterior rind surface.

**Matching analysis**:
- **Diplodia_stalk_rot**: "Numerous small black dots (pycnidia), about the size of a pinhead or smaller, can be observed in the lower internodes of the stalk" — **perfect match** for tiny black dots on stalk rind
- **Charcoal_stalk_rot**: Microsclerotia are internal on shredded pith — reference shows internal gray shredded tissue, not external dots on intact stalk
- **Tar_spot**: Black stromata are larger, raised, on leaves — reference shows on green leaf tissue
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot**: Shows shiny black patches/streaks, not tiny uniform dots
- **Southern_rust / Common_rust**: Orange/red pustules on leaves — eliminated
- **Eyespot**: Yellow-halo circular spots on green leaves — eliminated

The test image is unambiguously a stalk with the external rind covered in tiny black pycnidia — the hallmark of **Diplodia stalk rot**.

```json
{"prediction": "Diplodia_stalk_rot", "confidence": 0.88, "reasoning": "The image shows a corn stalk rind (tan-brown, intact, cylindrical) covered with numerous very tiny, uniformly distributed black dots — classic pycnidia of Diplodia zeae. This precisely matches the description 'Numerous small black dots (pycnidia), about the size of a pinhead or smaller, can be observed in the lower internodes of the stalk.' Charcoal stalk rot was ruled out (microsclerotia are internal on shredded pith), Tar spot (larger raised stromata on leaves), and Anthracnose stalk rot (shiny black patches/streaks rather than tiny dots)."}
```
